lines.label: PTAC exterior louver / architectural wall grille — the visible exterior face at each window
lines.where: Exterior face of each of the two PTAC sleeves — bedroom window and living-room window; visible from outside the building and through the unit's outdoor section
lines.instanceNote: FIVE STATEMENTS, NO RESOLUTION — reported exactly as each sheet reads, not merged. (1) M201 PTAC notes: 'polypropylene louver kit (color by architect)'. (2) M501 det.9: 'ALUMINUM ARCHITECTURAL-STYLE GRILLE FACTORY-PAINTED TO MATCH EXTERIOR WALL'. (3) M401 KN1: 'ARCHITECTURAL WALL GRILLE FURNISHED WITH UNIT; GRILLE PAINTED TO MATCH EXTERIOR WALL (TYPICAL FOR ALL PTAC UNITS)'. (4) A200 keyed note 8 verbatim: 'ALUMINUM FIXED WINDOW WITH THERMAL BROKEN FRAME, INSULATED GLAZING WITH INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS - SEE SHEET A-601 FOR SIZES' — i.e. part of the WINDOW system, the glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory. (5) AS103: 'INTEGRAL LOUVER TO BE INSTALLED WITH WINDOW SYSTEM'. The set disagrees on MATERIAL (polypropylene vs aluminium), on FINISH METHOD (architect-selected colour vs factory-painted vs painted to match) and on SCOPE (HVAC sub vs glazing sub). Polypropylene is moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted to an architect's colour, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. Compounding: A200/AS105 cite sheet A-601 for louver SIZES and A-601 IS NOT IN THE ISSUED SET (the set has A600 Doors and A610 Windows) — RFI R-04 — so the louver has no dimensional source either. SETTLES IT: one RFI to MWT / the M-EOR covering material, finish, colour and which sub buys it, plus the A601-to-A610 correction.

lines.verifyAtPunch: From outside, at BOTH windows of this suite: louver present, straight, fully seated, fastened, blades not crushed or missing, sealant to the wall/window joint continuous. RECORD the material actually installed (plastic vs aluminium) and the colour, and compare against the approved submittal before writing anything up. From inside: no daylight around the louver, no water staining below it. Walk the whole elevation at once — a mismatched louver only shows up in a row.

lines.label: Interior architectural wall grille at the PTAC, painted to match the INTERIOR wall (M401 KN5)
lines.where: Room-side face of each PTAC / sleeve — bedroom and living room

lines.label: PTAC thermostat — 7-day programmable, HARDWIRED (keynote 24 adds that thermostat-to-PTAC communication may be wireless). ONE PER PTAC, AND THIS ROOM HAS ONE PTAC — M401 states verbatim 'Each guestroom is served by a single PTAC', and A555 places keynote 1 only at the window wall, so expect ONE thermostat here
lines.where: Bedroom wall and living-room wall, near each PTAC. Exact location is deferred by BOTH mechanical sheets to the architectural set — M401 KN4 'refer architectural plans for exact location', M301 GN5 'refer arch/ID plans for exact thermostat location.' M101 N29 adds: not on an exterior wall if an interior wall is available; insulated backing plate if it must go on an exterior wall.
lines.instanceNote: THE COUNT QUESTION, ANSWERED — TWO, AND HERE IS WHY, WITH THE DISSENT RECORDED. The database carries ONE thermostat row for 202 (tagged 'PTAC 1'). The sheets support two: keynote 24 is PLACED TWICE across the A553 family, once on the bedroom side (A553.1, on its elevation set) and once on the living side (A553.2 view 01, the sofa wall). Those are two different rooms of one suite. Keynote 24 reads 'HARDWIRED THERMOSTAT FOR PTAC' — one thermostat per PTAC — and this key has two PTACs, which A553 states outright ('two TVs, two shades, two PTACs in one key'). That is repeated placement on a sheet, the same evidence standard packages/mechanical.md section 3 accepted for the second PTAC. THE DISSENT, CARRIED NOT SUPPRESSED: packages/electrical.md section 5.3 lists 'Second PTAC thermostat (kn24 placed x2 on A554)' as HIGH for 217/317/417 and, in its own words, 'not stated on A553' — because A554's ELECTRICAL PLAN draws the T symbol twice, whereas A553's electrical plan (view 04) carries kn24 in its keynote list without the transcription confirming a doubled symbol. So: two independent keynote placements in two rooms and two PTACs say TWO; the absence of a doubled T symbol on A553 view 04 is the only thing that says ONE, and a keynote list is not a symbol count. Emitted at 2 and FLAGGED so the walker settles it by counting. HEIGHT IS SEPARATELY NOT SETTLED — three values across five sources. 48": keynote 24 verbatim 'MOUNTED 48" MAX TO TOP OF DEVICE' (printed character-identical on all ten A550-A556 sheets, including A553/A553.1/A553.2), M101 GN29 '4'-0" AFF unless noted', G402 note 11 'ALL CONTROLS FOR USE BY GUESTS MUST BE MOUNTED BETWEEN 15" AFF AND 48" AFF'. 54": M401 KN4, for non-accessible rooms — and 202 is non-accessible — the only source for that number. 60": E101's symbol legend. coordination_issues.md C-03, live across all 115 rooms. DO NOT WRITE UP A HEIGHT DEFICIENCY ON THIS WALK — measure and record.
lines.src: A553 view 04 keyed note 24 · A553.1 keyed notes on the bedroom elevations (24) · A553.2 view 01 keyed note 24 · A550 keynote legend 24 (verbatim text) · M401 KN4 (54" non-accessible / 48" accessible) · M101 GN28 (controls scope split) + GN29 (4'-0" AFF) · M201 PTAC notes (7-day programmable) · M301 GN5 · E101 symbol legend (60" AFF) · G402 note 11 (15"-48") · packages/electrical.md section 5.3 (the dissent) · coordination_issues.md C-03
lines.verifyAtPunch: COUNT THE THERMOSTATS IN THE SUITE AND RECORD THE NUMBER — one or two, and which room each is in. That count is the deliverable from this line. Then at each: MEASURE and RECORD the height to the TOP of the device (that is how keynote 24 is written) against the three live values 48" / 54" / 60" — record, do not judge. Confirm hardwired and live; 7-day schedule programmable and the clock set; call for heat and call for cool and confirm THE PTAC IN THAT SAME ROOM responds (in a two-thermostat suite, cross-wired controls are the failure this test exists to catch); faceplate flush, level and clean. Check it is not on an exterior wall where an interior wall was available (M101 N29), and if it is on an exterior wall confirm the insulated backing plate.

lines.label: Aldes constant-airflow regulator at the 50 CFM ceiling exhaust inlet
lines.where: At the toilet exhaust ceiling inlet, immediately behind/above the EAG-50 grille
lines.instanceNote: The item is real and named — M305 states it verbatim at every inlet it draws ('CEILING GRILLE EXHAUST 50 CFM c/w ALDES CONSTANT AIRFLOW REGULATOR') and M302/M303/M304 repeat it for the typical floors, which includes floor 2. What is NOT established is that there is one in every guestroom, because the only sheet that scopes them does not add up: M305's seven riser totals sum to 2,450 CFM, which at 50 CFM per inlet is exactly 49 inlets, against roughly 119 needed (115 guestrooms + 4 ice-machine alcoves — M201 gives EF-1 area served as 'Toilet, ice machine'). M305 accounts for 41 percent of them. Independently, three of the four roof fans are scheduled BELOW the riser CFM assigned to them (EF-8 200 vs EV-1+EV-3 350; EF-9 300-350 vs EV-4+EV-5 650; EF-11 400-450 vs EV-2+EV-7 850; only EF-10/EV-6 balances at 600) — an 850 CFM aggregate shortfall. Either the seven risers drawn are a partial set or the riser CFM totals are wrong, and M305 does not say which. Which riser serves 202 is not determinable from the sheets in hand. SETTLES IT: the M-EOR reconciling the EV riser schedule against the room count and the roof-fan capacities. Until then, record presence/absence per room — field data points are real evidence for that RFI.

If present, confirm it is the correct nominal CFM and is seated in the duct, not loose. If absent, LOG IT — do not write it up as a deficiency until the EOR answers the riser arithmetic.

lines.instanceNote: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE READINGS. M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic FV-0511VK2 ceiling fan with remark 3 = 'switch w/ room lights', remark 5 = backdraft damper and remark 6 = off-white aluminium grille. M202, M301, M302, M303 and M304 all repeat EF-1 as the guest-toilet exhaust. But M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + ALDES REGULATOR on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 through EF-11 — no in-room fan anywhere. A grille-only inlet on a central riser and a dedicated in-room fan cannot both be true. Supporting but not conclusive: E400's Panel 'A' guestroom schedule (which is 202's panel — E400 detail 03 King One Bedroom is Panel A) carries circuits for Lighting, Convenience Receptacles, Bathroom GFCI, Refrigerator, Disposer, Dishwasher, Microwave/Hood, PTAC, Small Appliance and Spare, and NO exhaust-fan circuit — but M201 remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit and need no dedicated breaker. coordination_issues.md C-06. Do not order 115 Panasonic FV-0511VK2 on this. SETTLES IT: look up behind the bath grille and see whether there is a fan housing or an open duct to a riser.
lines.src: M201 exhaust fan schedule (EF-1 row, remarks 1,2,3,5,6,9) · M202 schematic · M301-M304 · vs M305 riser diagrams · E400 Panel 'A' schedule (detail 03 = King One Bedroom) · coordination_issues.md C-06
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look behind the bath ceiling grille and RECORD what is actually there — fan housing, or bare duct to a riser. That single observation closes C-06. If a fan is installed: operate it, record which switch controls it (M201 remark 3 says switched with the room lights), listen for the backdraft damper, confirm 50 CFM at the grille, confirm the grille finish is the off-white aluminium of remark 6. If no fan: confirm the grille still pulls 50 CFM off the central riser.

lines.label: Volume damper at the toilet exhaust, with a locking quadrant
lines.where: At the toilet exhaust branch. M401 does not dimension its position; M101's legend defines VD as a manual volume damper, M101 GN25/GN26 require each outlet to have its own balancing device with a locking quadrant, and M301 GN11 requires a balancing damper at each branch/runout.
lines.instanceNote: SCOPE CALL. If the VD sits at the grille neck it is reachable by dropping the EAG-50 and is plainly IN. If it sits further up the branch it is above the 7'-3" hard painted-gyp lid with NO access panel drawn on any guestroom RCP — including A553 view 02 — and it becomes unreachable rough-in. No sheet says which. Carried IN under the arguable-call rule because the damper's EFFECT is tested at a visible point (the airflow reading at the grille) and because M101 GN7 requires access to it in either case. SETTLES IT: drop the grille and look; and the same RFI that asks for the missing bath access panel.
lines.src: M401 (EAG-50 shown with VD and FD) · M101 legend + GN25/GN26 · M301 GN11 · M101 GN7 (access panels min 12"x12" to dampers)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Drop the EAG-50 and look up the neck for a damper with a locking quadrant. If it is there: reachable, set and locked, not wired shut or fully closed. If it is not visible at the neck, RECORD that it is above the hard lid with no access — that is the access-panel finding, not a damper finding. Either way take the airflow reading at the grille against 50 CFM; that is the real test of the setting.

lines.label: Wall air grille / make-up air diffuser, 30 CFM — the transfer/make-up air path to the bathroom (keynote 20, 'MAKE-UP AIR DIFFUSER')
lines.where: CONTESTED, AND THIS ROOM TYPE PLACES IT SOMEWHERE UNEXPECTED. M401 describes WAG-30 as a transfer grille providing make-up air TO THE BATH. On this type keynote 20 is placed on A553.2 VIEW 02 — the DINING NOOK elevation in the living room — which is not a bath wall and is not even in the same room as the bath.
lines.instanceNote: TWO SEPARATE UNCERTAINTIES ON ONE ITEM, PLUS A ROOM-TYPE-SPECIFIC ONE. (1) TAG: like EAG-50, 'WAG-30' is a callout in M101's designation/CFM format (wall air grille @ 30 CFM), not a schedule mark — M201's Titus schedule has no WAG-30 row and the crosswalk to any Titus mark is un-made (coordination_issues.md S-02). Architectural corroborates the DEVICE but not the tag: keynote 20 reads 'MAKE-UP AIR DIFFUSER' with no tag on it. (2) LOCATION ON THIS TYPE: A553.2 places keynote 20 on view 02, the dining-nook elevation. A553's own view 01 (architectural plan) keyed-note list does NOT carry 20, and A553.1 (all four bedroom elevations) does not carry 20 either. So on the King One Bedroom the only placement of the make-up air diffuser in the whole sheet family is on a living-room dining wall, while M401 says its job is to make up air to the bath. That may be right (a transfer path from the living room), it may be a placement error, and it may mean the bedroom — a separate room behind a door (GR-4) with its own PTAC — has no make-up air path drawn at all. (3) COUNT: one placement is drawn, so qty 1; whether a two-room suite behind a closed interior door needs a second transfer is not addressed by any sheet. M301 GN13 permits a lined transfer duct OR a door undercut where make-up air is under 50 CFM, and M101's legend defines an undercut door at 1/2", but no sheet places an undercut at any door in this suite, so no undercut is claimed here. SETTLES IT: field observation on this walk (where is the grille actually installed, and is there anything at the bedroom or bath), plus the M-EOR confirming the location for this type.
lines.src: M401 (WAG-30, 30 CFM, make-up to the bath) · A553.2 view 02 keynote 20 (the only placement in the A553 family) · A553 view 01 and A553.1 — keynote 20 NOT placed · M301 GN13 (transfer duct or door undercut under 50 CFM) · M101 legend (undercut door UC 1/2") · coordination_issues.md S-02
lines.verifyAtPunch: Walk the whole suite and RECORD WHERE THE MAKE-UP AIR GRILLE ACTUALLY IS — dining nook wall, bath wall, bedroom, or absent — and how many there are. Confirm it is fastened, square, blades undamaged, painted to match its wall and not overspray-blinded. Airflow read against 30 CFM. Then the functional test: shut the bath door and the bedroom door with the bath exhaust running and confirm the bath can still pull air; if the bath starves with the bedroom door shut, that is the finding this line exists to catch.

lines.label: Access panel in the bath ceiling to the fire damper and volume damper — required by note, drawn on NO guestroom reflected ceiling plan
lines.where: Would be in the 7'-3" PT-07 painted-gypsum bath lid, at the FD/VD above it
lines.instanceNote: ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROW — emitted because its PRESENCE OR ABSENCE is exactly what a walker sees standing in a finished bathroom, and because the requirement is printed even though the placement is not. M101 GN7 requires access panels in ceilings/walls to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts and controls, min 12"x12". M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC unit maintenance. M501 requires fire/smoke dampers to have approved access with a permanent exterior label in letters at least 1/2" high reading FIRE DAMPER / SMOKE DAMPER / FIRE-SMOKE DAMPER. NONE of the ten A550-A556 guestroom RCPs draws one, A553 view 02 included — its RCP keynotes are 31 (x3), 18, 19, 4 and 1, and no access panel among them. The only flush-access-panel keynote anywhere in the A12x/A55x set is A121 keynote 5, at the ICE-MACHINE alcove, not in a guestroom. This is a real, repeating, 115-room omission, an RFI candidate and a CO-inspection exposure — an inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. Not invented: the requirement is printed, only the placement is missing.
lines.src: M101 GN7 · M301 Key Note 4 · M501 (fire/smoke damper access + permanent exterior label) · M101 GN31/GN32 · against A553 view 02 (RCP keynotes 31, 18, 19, 4, 1 — no access panel) · A121 keynote 5 (the only flush-access-panel keynote in the set, at the ice-machine alcove)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look at the bath ceiling: is there an access panel? RECORD YES or NO. If yes — min 12"x12", flush, latching, finished/painted, and carrying the permanent damper label required by M101 GN31/GN32 in letters at least 1/2" high. If no — that is the finding; photograph the intact lid. CUT NOTHING.

lines.label: Guestroom panelboard — 100 A MCB, 120/208 V 1-phase 3-wire, NEMA 1, copper bus (Square D / GE / Cutler-Hammer). E400 detail 03 is the King One Bedroom and puts it on PANEL A, not Panel B
lines.where: TWO SHEETS PUT IT IN TWO DIFFERENT ROOMS — see instanceNote. A553.2 view 03 labels 'ELEC. PANEL' at the left (entry) end of the WORKING WALL, keynote 51; E400's Panel A schedule header states Location: BEDROOM. In a two-room suite those are not the same place.
lines.instanceNote: THREE THINGS TO SETTLE AT ONE PANEL DOOR. (1) LOCATION CONFLICT: keynote 51 'ELECTRICAL PANEL' is placed on A553 view 04 and labelled 'ELEC. PANEL' on the working-wall elevation A553.2 view 03 — i.e. in the LIVING room at the entry end. E400's Panel A schedule header prints Location: Bedroom. Both recorded; neither resolved. In this suite the answer also drives millwork access clearance, because the working wall is casework and A553.2's own PM note calls the panel-door-versus-casework-face collision a classic late-punch item. (2) ROOM-TYPE CONFLICT ON THE FEEDER SHEET: E103.3's PANEL 2B items-served summary names 'RM 222 PNL A King One Bedroom' and puts 'RM 202/204/206/208/210/212' down as KING STUDIO. That is the reverse of the plan of record — A101 / room_map.md make 202 the King One Bedroom and 222 a King Studio (222 also carries a stale superseded '213' tag buried under its number box). Architectural governs room numbering, and OPEN_ITEMS records separately that E103's room-type rows are not trustworthy as a census — but the discrepancy is live and it is readable off the panel directory. (3) PANEL A vs B: Panel B is the accessible/motorized-shade panel; 202 is non-accessible and carries GR-400 MANUAL shades, so no shade circuit and Panel A. NOTE: the branch circuits themselves (lighting, convenience receptacles, bath GFCI, refrigerator, disposer, dishwasher, microwave/hood, PTAC, small appliance 1 and 2, spare) are concealed rough-in and are dropped per scope — but every one of them is a breaker you can see with the door open, which is why the checks are folded into this line.
lines.src: E400 detail 03 (King One Bedroom, Panel A) + Panel 'A' schedule and its four panel notes · E101 GN #10 (Square D/GE/Cutler-Hammer, copper bus only) · E101 #31 / E400 notes 2 and 3 (AFCI) / note 4 (GFCI breaker) · A553 view 04 keynote 51 · A553.2 view 03 'ELEC. PANEL' · E103.3 Panel 2B items-served (the room-type conflict) · A101 / room_map.md line 91 and 108 (202 = King One Bedroom, 222 = King Studio)
lines.verifyAtPunch: RECORD WHICH ROOM THE PANEL IS ACTUALLY IN — bedroom or living-room working wall. Open the door: directory typed, legible and correct, and READ WHAT ROOM NUMBER AND ROOM TYPE IT IS LABELLED WITH (that is what closes the E103.3 202-vs-222 discrepancy). Confirm the AFCI breakers and the GFCI breaker per E400 panel notes 2, 3 and 4, and that a spare/space exists. Cover flush and square to the finished wall, no gap to the millwork, door opens fully WITHOUT fouling the casework face, working clearance in front not blocked by furniture or the closet. No unlabelled or hand-scrawled circuits.

lines.label: Vanity wall sconce — Arkansas Lighting 3550V, LED, wall mounted (E101 row verbatim: "WS03 | Wall sconce — guestroom vanity | Arkansas Lighting 3550V | Wall | LED")
lines.where: Bathroom vanity wall, at the vanity mirror. A531 view 05 is the vanity wall and carries keynote 12 'vanity mirror & light fixture'; the plan tags GR-203 vanity sconce.

A531 places GR-203 'VANITY SCONE [sic]' once on its plan and keynote 12 once on view 05, so one is emitted; the suite bath is substantially larger than the studio bath (12'-0 1/2" x 9'-0 1/2" clear against A530's smaller footprint) and GR-302 is tagged 'VANITY @GUEST BATH (LEFT&RIGHT)', so a second fixture would not be surprising. COUNT AND RECORD. SEPARATE OPEN ITEM — BUYOUT RISK: E101 schedules WS03 (Arkansas 3550V) as a base-build ELECTRICAL vanity sconce while the FF&E set schedules GR-203 Vanity Sconce on every bath sheet (A530-A533 keynote 12, ID-5.10-5.13). lines.src: E101 fixture schedule (S21 / WS01 / WS03 rows) · E400 (WS03 vanity) · A531 view 05 keynote 12 + GR-203 tag on plan 01 · A550 furnishings legend GR-203 · packages/electrical.md section 4 row 24 and open item 4

Fixture level, centred on the mirror/vanity, canopy tight to the wall with no gap or gap-filler caulk smear, lamped and lit from the room switch, lens/diffuser clean and undamaged, no finger marks on the finish. lines.where: Bedroom headboard wall, one over each nightstand (GR-319 nightstand @ right, GR-323 nightstand @ left). A553.1 view 02 is that wall — WC-01 wallcovering behind the headboard.

Included in the electrical punch because it is a wall-mounted light fixture in a finished room even though it is bought on the FF&E package. lines.label: Bath ceiling surface-mount downlight — Cooper Halo SMD6R69SWH, LED (E101 row verbatim: "S21 | Surface mount downlight — guestroom restroom")
lines.where: Bathroom ceiling, 7'-3" PT-07 gyp lid

The suite bath is materially larger than the studio bath it was scheduled against, so one may not be the real number here. COUNT AND RECORD. Note E101 describes S21 as SURFACE MOUNT, which is why it is a separate line from the RECESSED wet-location fixture at the shower (keynote 18) — see that line; the two are different fixtures and only one of them has a schedule type.

Each seated flat to the lid with no gap or shadow line, lamped and lit from the bath switch, lens clean, no paint on the trim, no drywall dust inside the lens. lines.label: Recessed WET-LOCATION ceiling light over the shower, with shatter-proof lens — keyed note 18 verbatim: 'RECESSED CEILING LIGHT FOR WET LOCATIONS W/ SHATTER PROOF LENS'
lines.where: Bathroom ceiling over the shower. Keynote 18 is placed on A553 view 02 (the RCP).
lines.instanceNote: THE FIXTURE IS REQUIRED BUT HAS NO SCHEDULE TYPE. Keynote 18 places a RECESSED wet-location fixture at the shower; E101's only guestroom-bath fixture is S21, which is SURFACE MOUNT. So the fixture the architect keynotes at the shower is not the fixture the engineer scheduled, and no type, model or trim exists for it anywhere in the set. Logged as packages/electrical.md open item 3, RFI. Governing requirements that DO exist: E101 spec Note (1) — a luminaire over a tub or shower must be enclosed, gasketed and wet-location listed per NEC 550.14(D); E400 GN #5 — fixtures over wet areas damp-rated. Do not accept an ordinary recessed can over the shower on the strength of the missing schedule row.
lines.src: A553 view 02 keynote 18 · A550 keynote legend 18 (verbatim) · E101 spec Note (1) (NEC 550.14(D), enclosed/gasketed/wet-location listed) · E400 GN #5 · packages/electrical.md open item 3
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look up in the shower: fixture present, RECESSED, lens intact and SHATTER-PROOF, gasket seated, trim tight to the ceiling with no gap. READ THE LABEL AND RECORD THE MAKE, MODEL AND THE WET-LOCATION / DAMP-LOCATION LISTING — that record is what fills the missing schedule row. Switch it and confirm it lights. Any sign of moisture inside the lens is a finding.

lines.label: Entry, closet and general room lighting fixtures — TYPE NEVER NAMED ON ANY SHEET
lines.where: Entry vestibule, closet, bedroom and living room. A553 view 04 prints 'CENTER OVER CLOSET' at the entry closet and a second 'CENTER ... CLOSET' note in the bedroom, so at least two of these fixtures are dimensionally located over closets.
lines.instanceNote: QTY IS A PLACEHOLDER OF 1 — THE COUNT IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE AND WAS NOT INVENTED. E400 shows entry/closet/general room lighting present in the typical guestroom but names no fixture type, and E101's schedule has no row for it (S21 is the bath downlight, WS03 the vanity sconce, WS01 the corridor sconce). packages/electrical.md open item 2 records it flatly: 'Guestroom entry / closet / general lighting fixture type never named on any sheet — OPEN. RFI.' A553's RCP (view 02) carries keynotes 31, 18, 19, 4 and 1 and no general-lighting keynote, so the plan gives no count either. THIS SUITE HAS MORE OF THEM THAN ANY OTHER KEY — two habitable rooms plus an entry vestibule plus a closet at 6'-2" clear, against one room in a studio — so a count taken here is worth more than a count taken anywhere else. The walker's count IS the deliverable.
lines.src: E400 (present, untyped) · E101 fixture schedule (no matching row) · A553 view 04 'CENTER OVER CLOSET' notes · A553 view 02 RCP (no general-lighting keynote) · packages/electrical.md section 4 row 22 and open item 2

Each: switched and lit, trim tight, level, lens clean, correct lamp colour temperature consistent room to room (a mismatched lamp between the bedroom and living room of one suite is visible from the connecting door). Confirm the closet fixtures are centred over the closets per the A553 view 04 notes.

Fixture switched, lit, level, trim tight. If no fixture is there, RECORD IT — the note is the only thing that requires it, and the absence is the finding.

lines.label: Bathroom GFCI duplex receptacle, tamper-resistant, 20 A, on a sidewall of the water basin
lines.where: Bath vanity, sidewall of the basin (G402 general note 6). A531 view 05 annotates it as free text 'GFI' rather than using keyed note 13.
lines.instanceNote: COUNT NOT PRINTED for this type — one is emitted because one is the annotated condition on A531 view 05 and G402 note 6 states the requirement in the singular ('GFCI duplex outlet on a sidewall of the water basin'). Two notations for the same device exist across the bath sheet set (keyed note 13 elsewhere, free text 'GFI' on A531) — recorded, not resolved, per A531 flag 3. Device rules that bind it: E101 #25 and GN #6 — all 120 V 15/20 A non-locking receptacles in guestrooms and guest baths TAMPER-RESISTANT; E101 GN #10 — all receptacles and switches 20 A per local amendment; E400 note 4 — GFCI breaker at the panel. G402 note 1 / E400 GN #2 permit it to share a common 4x4 box with the light switch.
lines.src: A530-A533 keyed note 13 · A531 view 05 'GFI' free-text annotation · G402 general note 6 · E400 Panel 'A' Bathroom GFCI circuit + note 4 · E101 #25 / GN #6 / GN #10
lines.verifyAtPunch: Push TEST — the receptacle must trip; push RESET — it must restore, and plug a tester in to confirm correct polarity and ground both before and after. Confirm the device face reads TR (tamper-resistant) and that it is on a sidewall of the basin, not behind it. Plate flush, level, unpainted. If protection is at the breaker rather than the device, confirm the breaker trips on the tester and RECORD which arrangement is installed.

lines.label: Convenience duplex receptacles throughout the suite — tamper-resistant, 20 A, AFCI-protected, centreline 18" AFF
lines.where: Bedroom, living room, dining nook, entry and working wall. A553 view 04 carries the device-spacing dimension string (8'-2", 7'-0", 4'-2", 3'-3", 3'-0", 2'-11 3/4", 2'-11", 2'-3", 2'-0", 1'-9", 1'-4", 18", 10", 8", 6", 5", 4", 3") but the symbols are graphics and no count is printed.

The database's own row says it outright: 'count per room is NOT STATED on any sheet.' A553 view 04 draws the devices and dimensions their spacing, but a dimension string is not a count and the symbols were not counted off the sheet. THE COUNT IS THE DELIVERABLE FROM THIS LINE, and it matters more on this key than any other: this is a two-room suite with a dining nook and the largest working wall in the building, so a receptacle count carried over from a King Studio will be short. THE RULE THAT DOES BIND EVERY ONE OF THEM, printed on A553 view 04 verbatim: 'BACK TO BACK DEVICES: ALL DEVICES SHALL BE OFFSET SO THAT NO DEVICE IN ADJACENT GUESTROOM ARE BACK TO BACK' — E101 #28 puts numbers on it (max box 4"x4" in a rated wall, 6" separation non-rated, 24" separation fire/acoustic-rated) and E101 #29 requires putty pads at back-to-back receptacle boxes. HEIGHT: E101 #18 and the symbol legend both give receptacles at 18" AFF; A553.1 view 02 separately calls 1'-6" on the headboard wall, which agrees.
lines.src: A553 view 04 (device symbols, spacing dimensions, and the BACK TO BACK DEVICES note verbatim) · E101 #18 (receptacles +18" AFF) · E101 #25 (tamper-resistant) · E101 #31 / E400 notes 2 and 3 (AFCI) · E101 GN #10 (20 A devices, #12 min) · E101 #28 and #29 (box separation, putty pads) · A553.1 view 02 (1'-6")
lines.verifyAtPunch: COUNT AND RECORD THE RECEPTACLES ROOM BY ROOM — bedroom, living room, dining nook, entry, working wall. Then test every one with a plug tester: correct wiring, ground present, and confirm the AFCI trips and resets from the panel. Every device face must read TR. Spot-measure two or three centrelines against 18" AFF. All plates flush, level, unpainted and uncracked, no gap to the finished wall or to the millwork.

lines.label: Extended J-box with device and cover plate flush with the millwork back panel — keynote 25 verbatim: 'EXTEND J-BOX, DEVICE & COVER PLATE FLUSH W/ MILLWORK BACK PANEL'

lines.label: TV outlet at the LIVING-ROOM television (FF&E tag 903) — coax behind the TV plus a CAT6 RJ-45 jack behind the TV run in smurf tube in the wall to the WAP under the desk, patch cord to the Connected Room edge controller

lines.label: Wired data connection at the desktop grommet — keynote 46 verbatim: 'OPTION WIRED DATA CONNECTION FOR GUEST USE: A) ADD CAT6 RJ-45 CABLE JACK AND PATCH CORD THROUGH DESKTOP GROMMET - OR - B) PATCH CORD FROM WAP PORT THROUGH DESKTOP GROMMET'

Photograph it. If A or B, test it live. Log the answer — it is the same answer on all 115 keys and it is worth knowing before someone prices it.

lines.label: Wireless access point in a 3-GANG BOX MOUNTED VERTICALLY under the desk — keynote 44 verbatim: 'WAP IN 3-GANG BOX MOUNTED VERTICALLY UNDER DESK. MAINTAIN 6" BETWEEN ALL BOXES, TYP ALL GUESTROOMS. COORDINATE WAP LOCATION WITH CASEGOODS TO AVOID CONFLICTS'

Whether one WAP covers the bedroom through that partition is a commissioning question, not a drawing question, and no sheet addresses it. RECORD SIGNAL IN THE BEDROOM. Unit secured, ventilated, not buried where housekeeping will unplug it, cabling labelled. If none is present and both TVs work, record that too and let the integrator explain the topology.

lines.label: Doorbell on/off switch — kn28 verbatim: 'DOORBELL ON/OFF SWITCH (COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS ONLY) SIGNAGE AS REQ'D.' COMMUNICATION-FEATURES KEYS ONLY.

lines.where: Shower control wall

That is the pressure-balance test and it is the whole point of the valve. Then confirm the handle turns fully off with no drip, moves smoothly through its arc, the escutcheon is tight and sealed, and the hot side is on the left.

lines.label: Floor drain, guest bathroom — 2" per the P301-series general notes; "MAINTAIN ACCESSIBLE COMPLIANT SLOPES TO DRAIN". No guestroom floor drain is scheduled anywhere in P104
lines.where: Bath floor. Keyed note 20 is placed on the A531 plan; A553 view 01's keynote legend also defines keynote 6 as FLOOR DRAIN.
lines.instanceNote: TWO SHEETS DISAGREE AND BOTH READINGS ARE CARRIED. P402 lists the floor drain among the fixtures served in ACCESSIBLE units; A531 keyed note 20 places one on the KING ONE BEDROOM bath plan, which is the plan that governs 202 and which is a non-accessible key. Neither is resolved here. SEPARATELY, THE GUESTROOM FLOOR DRAIN HAS NO MARK AND NO SCHEDULED PRODUCT — P104's Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule carries FD-1 (Mechanical/Laundry, Zurn Z550), FD-2 (Unfinished Spaces, Zurn Z415B) and FD-3 (Funnel, Zurn Z514E) and none is a guestroom drain, so no make, model or strainer finish is specified for the item the walker is standing over. SETTLES IT: MWT CA confirming whether the non-accessible baths receive a floor drain, plus the FD submittal naming the product. Recording present/absent room by room answers the first half by itself.
lines.src: A531 plan 01 keyed note 20 · A530 kn20 (same text) · A550/A553 keynote legend 6 ('FLOOR DRAIN') · P402 ('floor drain (FD)' listed in ACCESSIBLE units) · P301 general note (floor drain 2") · P104 drain schedule (no guestroom row) · packages/plumbing.md section 6A row 14
lines.verifyAtPunch: RECORD PRESENT or ABSENT. If present: pour a cup of water at each corner of the bath floor and watch it reach the drain — that is the 'accessible compliant slopes' test, and E400 GN #4 caps the slope at 1:48 in any direction. Strainer secure, drain flush with the tile and not proud, no ponding left behind after the floor dries.

lines.label: Trap guard / trap primer at the bathroom floor drain — the primer valve body is concealed but the trap guard is visible through the strainer and the seal is testable
lines.where: At the bath floor drain — reachable by lifting the strainer
lines.instanceNote: TWO DIFFERENT PRIMER PRODUCTS ARE SCHEDULED AND NEITHER IS SCOPED TO A GUESTROOM: P104 schedules TP-1 = PPP SMP-500-115V (scoped to a 6" sump-pump standpipe, not a guest bath), while P102 schedules the Automatic Trap Primer Valve as Sioux Chief 695 Series, 30-250 PSIG, 'installed in accessible locations per notes (NPCA/ASSE 1018)'. Meanwhile P301 general note 6 requires a trap guard or primer at EVERY floor drain, repeated on P302-P310, and P501 detail 12 details it. This line follows the floor-drain line — if there is no FD in 202, there is no trap guard or primer either. A dry trap in a finished, unoccupied hotel room is the exact failure this exists to prevent, and it is a smell complaint on day one of occupancy.
lines.src: P301 general note 6 (repeated P302-P310) · P501 detail 12 · P102 Automatic Trap Primer Valve Schedule (Sioux Chief 695 Series) · P104 TP-1 (PPP SMP-500-115V) · packages/plumbing.md section 6A row 15
lines.verifyAtPunch: Lift the strainer and look into the drain body for a trap guard — RECORD PRESENT or ABSENT and any manufacturer marking on it. Pour water and confirm the seal holds. Then check again on a later pass for evaporation or sewer odour, and note whether the room is being aired or sealed between now and turnover.

lines.label: PTAC condensate drain — 1" VISIBLE drain with a 1" AIR-GAP FITTING, 1" condensate line with a 1-1/2" vent up, to the 4" condensate main. TWO PTACs IN THIS KEY MEANS TWO CONDENSATE DROPS.
lines.where: At each PTAC, in the wall below the unit — the visible drain and its air-gap fitting are the punchable part; the in-wall piping to the riser is concealed and excluded
lines.instanceNote: QTY 2 IS DERIVED FROM THE TWO PTACs, NOT FROM A PLUMBING SHEET — and that is exactly why it is flagged. P302-P304 and P501 det.13 describe the condensate arrangement generically, M301 GN6 requires full-size condensate from EACH packaged AC unit to the 2" condensate riser, and M401 KN2 assigns the piping to plumbing ('typical for all PTAC units'). No plumbing sheet states a SECOND condensate drop for the King One Bedroom, and packages/plumbing.md open item 3 confirms fixture counts per unit were not extracted from P401/P402 plan 06 (the King One Bdr plan). So: two units require two drops by M301 GN6's own wording, but the plumbing set has not been shown to draw the second one. If only one drop exists in this suite, one PTAC is draining nowhere — which is a wet-wall and a stained-elevation problem, not a punch-list nicety. NOTE ALSO the two sheet-number typos on P301: it points to the condensate dry-well detail as 'P502' when the detail is on P501.
lines.src: M301 General Note 6 (full-size condensate from EACH packaged AC unit) · M401 KN2 · M501 det.9 · P302-P304 · P501 detail 13 · packages/plumbing.md section 6A row 16 and open item 3 · coordination_issues.md X-03 (P301 sheet-number typos)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Run BOTH PTACs in cooling long enough to make condensate, then CONFIRM AT EACH UNIT SEPARATELY that water is actually leaving through its own drain — not pooling in the pan, not weeping into the room, not running down the outside face. Find and RECORD the 1" air-gap fitting at each: if you can only find one drop for two units, that is the finding and it needs the M-EOR and the plumbing sub the same day. Check the wall and carpet below both units and the ceiling of the room beneath for staining.

lines.label: Gate valves at the CWS, HWS and HWR riser take-offs — one at each of the three risers, with unions, behind an 18"x18" access panel
lines.where: Guestroom wet wall / plumbing stack. WHERE THE PANEL PHYSICALLY LANDS IS THE OPEN QUESTION — P502 det.3 draws it in a SUSPENDED ceiling and no ceiling in this suite is suspended (A553 view 02: PT-07 painted gypsum at 8'-3 3/8" in both rooms and 7'-3" at bath and entry).
lines.instanceNote: SCOPE: P101 note 9 reads verbatim 'Furnish access panels (installed by GC) as required' and sits in the PLUMBING general notes — so the PLUMBING contractor FURNISHES the panel and the GC INSTALLS it. Name both parties before the walk; on a line whose point is 'if there is NO panel, write it up', getting that backwards is the difference between a back-charge and an own-cost fix. WHY IT IS OPEN: P502 det.3 draws an 18"x18" panel in a suspended ceiling, no guestroom ceiling in this set is suspended, and no access-panel symbol or keyed note is drawn on A553 view 02 or anywhere else in the A553 family. SEPARATE VALVE-TYPE CONFLICT, BOTH READINGS CARRIED: P401 and P502 draw a GATE valve; P101 GN15 specifies BALL valves or approved equal. The database carries three separate GV rows; collapsed to one line at qty 3 because the walker opens one panel and looks at three valves.
lines.src: P401 Domestic Water Typical Unit (a GV at each of the three riser take-offs) · P502 detail 3 (Shut-Off Valve Installation Detail, 18"x18" access panel in a suspended ceiling) · P101 general note 9 (verbatim) · P101 note 15 (ball valves or approved equal, located accessibly) · M101 GN7 (min 12"x12" access to valves) · A553 view 02 (no suspended ceiling, no access panel drawn)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Find the access panel and RECORD WHERE IT IS (bedroom ceiling / bath ceiling / entry / corridor outside the door). Open it: three valves with unions; cycle each fully closed and fully open — a valve that will not turn is the classic finding — and confirm no weep at stems or unions after cycling. RECORD GATE vs BALL. If there is no panel anywhere in the suite, write that up against P101 note 15 and M101 GN7.

lines.label: Kitchenette / wet-bar sink and faucet — P401 verbatim: 'a kitchenette/wet-bar sink (SK-3 / SK-4) IN THE SUITE/EXTENDED UNITS'; P402 verbatim: 'SK-3 / SK-4 (kitchenette/wet-bar sink IN SUITES/EXTENDED UNITS)'. Product only from unstamped cutsheets: American Standard PEKOE 18SB.10231800.075 undermount with Moen 8227 faucet.
lines.where: Working wall at the kitchenette, between the refrigerator (901) and dishwasher (902), under the microwave (keynote 11). The disposal switch (keynote 14) and dedicated disposal circuit (keynote 15) both land here.
lines.instanceNote: OF ALL 115 KEYS, THIS IS THE ONE THE PHRASE MOST PLAUSIBLY MEANS — AND IT IS STILL NOT STATED. P401 and P402 restrict SK-3/SK-4 to 'the suite/extended units' and then assign it to NONE of the seven unit plans they draw, while P104 schedules no product for either mark. The phrase is doubly ambiguous on this job because Home2 brands EVERY key a 'suite', so it may mean all rooms or only plans 06/07 (King One Bdr and King One Bdr Acc.) plus the Ext variant. Room 202 IS plan 06, the King One Bedroom, so if the narrow reading is right this room is one of the six keys that carries it. That is a reading, not a ruling — FLAGGED. Compounding: the electrical set draws a disposal switch (kn14) and a DEDICATED DISPOSAL CIRCUIT (kn15, 480 VA on Panel A) and a dedicated dishwasher circuit on this same wall, and packages/plumbing.md says it plainly — 'A dishwasher with no drawn sink is itself an RFI.' PRODUCT WARNING: the S4 'Kitchenette Faucet' file is on its face a two-handle 8" WIDESPREAD LAVATORY faucet, 3-hole, which will not drop into a single-hole undermount deck. RFI to the MEP EOR: which unit types receive a kitchenette sink?
lines.src: P401 verbatim · P402 verbatim · P104 (no scheduled product for SK-3 or SK-4; its SK-1/SK-2 are both laundry sinks) · S4 product data (PEKOE 18SB.10231800.075, 23x18 single-bowl SS undermount, 18 ga, 10" deep, 26" cabinet required, bottom grid 7302282-401.0750A, waste 9028000.075, clips 791676-100.0070A; Moen 8227) · A553 view 01 and A553.2 view 03 (901, 902, keynotes 11, 14, 15) · packages/plumbing.md section 7
lines.verifyAtPunch: RECORD WHETHER A KITCHENETTE SINK EXISTS IN THIS SUITE — that single yes/no on plan 06 is the best field evidence available for the open SK-3/SK-4 RFI. If present: run hot and cold, fill and drain, no weep at the tailpiece, trap, supplies or disposer collar; undermount clips tight and the counter joint sealed; disposer runs from the ganged switch and is quiet with no rattle; RECORD the sink and faucet models and whether the faucet is single-hole or widespread. If absent: photograph the dishwasher, the disposal switch and the disposal circuit sitting there with no sink, and send it with the RFI.

lines.label: Addressable photoelectric smoke detector — Silent Knight SKPHOTOW head in a System Sensor B200S-LF-WH LOW-FREQUENCY (520 Hz) sounder base. Detector 1 of 2 — LIVING ROOM
lines.where: Living-room ceiling. A553.2 view 02 (dining nook) shows an SD symbol on the living side.
lines.instanceNote: TWO DETECTORS IN THIS KEY IS SETTLED, NOT ASSUMED. FA-3 was read at 450-500 dpi on room 317 (KING ONE BEDROOM ACCESSIBLE) and shows two — one in the living room (PS3-1-2 / L2-D-33) and one in the bedroom (PS3-1-1 / L2-D-32). That closes the schedule arithmetic exactly: FA-1 schedules 121 SKPHOTOW heads and 121 B200S-LF-WH bases, and 115 keys + 6 second detectors in the 6 one-bedroom units (3 King One Bedroom + 3 King One Bedroom Acc.) = 121. The second head is drawn, not inferred. THE SOUNDER BASE IS THE AUDIBLE APPLIANCE FOR THIS SLEEPING ROOM — a corridor horn does not satisfy it; FA-1's audibility chart gives sleeping rooms 35 dBA ambient, 75 dBA design, low frequency, visual required. Each head carries two addresses, an SLC address and a NAC/power-supply circuit. The vendor submittal (Security Integrated Inc, Hilton A/D&C REVIEWED 04/29/2025) GOVERNS over the E-series on device counts — conflicts.md B1.9 and E500's own gap note both defer the device-by-device bill to this performance design.
lines.src: FA-1 Fire Alarm Equipment Schedule row (S)SB, qty 121/121 · FA-3 room 317 read head-by-head (living PS3-1-2 / L2-D-33) · A553.2 view 02 (SD symbol) · A553.1 view 03 (SD symbol) · E500 FA note 10 (FA boxes and cover plates painted red) · packages/fire-appliance.md sections 2.2 and 2.4
lines.verifyAtPunch: Head seated in its base with no shipping cap, LED in normal state, no paint, drywall dust or overspray on head, base or chamber. Then with the FA vendor put it in test: the head alarms, THE LOW-FREQUENCY BASE SOUNDS IN THIS ROOM, and the FACP annunciates ROOM 202 with both its SLC and NAC addresses read back to you. Any exposed emergency-system junction box or cover plate must be PAINTED RED per E500 note 10.

lines.label: Addressable photoelectric smoke detector on a low-frequency sounder base — Silent Knight SKPHOTOW in System Sensor B200S-LF-WH. Detector 2 of 2 — BEDROOM
lines.where: Bedroom ceiling. A553.1 view 03 (bedroom door / full-length mirror wall) shows the SD symbol with the horn.
lines.instanceNote: THE SECOND DETECTOR IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ROOM TYPE'S FIRE-ALARM DELTA. The bedroom is a separate sleeping room behind a full-height partition and a door (GR-4) — a detector in the living room cannot cover it and its sounder base cannot wake someone through a closed door. FA-3's read of room 317 draws it (PS3-1-1 / L2-D-32) and the 121-device schedule arithmetic requires it. If a fire-alarm takeoff counted 115 detectors by key instead of 121 by room, this is the device that went missing, and it went missing in the room where somebody sleeps. Verify it exists before anything else on this line.
lines.src: FA-1 Fire Alarm Equipment Schedule (121 heads / 121 bases) · FA-3 room 317 read head-by-head (bedroom PS3-1-1 / L2-D-32) · A553.1 view 03 (SD symbol) · A553 view 01 (GR-4 bedroom-to-living door) · packages/fire-appliance.md section 2.2
lines.verifyAtPunch: CONFIRM A SECOND DETECTOR EXISTS IN THE BEDROOM — if it does not, stop and report it, because that is a life-safety miss and it repeats on 302 and 402. If it does: head seated, no shipping cap, LED normal, clean. Put it in test with the vendor: head alarms, THE BASE SOUNDS IN THE BEDROOM WITH THE GR-4 DOOR CLOSED and is read at 75 dBA at the pillow, and the FACP annunciates room 202 with its own distinct SLC address, different from the living-room head.

lines.label: Fire horn — keynote 16 verbatim: 'FIRE HORN IN STANDARD ROOMS / FIRE HORN/STROBE IN COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS'. 202 is a standard key, so the architectural set would give it horns, not horn/strobes.
lines.where: A553.1 view 03 (bedroom) and A553.2 views 01 and 02 (living / dining) all place keynote 16 and show H symbols — i.e. the architectural set draws one in each room of the suite
lines.instanceNote: A STRAIGHT DOCUMENT CONFLICT ON A DEVICE VISIBLE FROM THE DOORWAY — QTY IS EITHER 2 OR 0, AND THE DATABASE CARRIES NEITHER (it holds only the two smoke-detector rows). FOR: the architectural permit set places keynote 16 three times across the A553 family and draws H symbols beside the SDs on A553.1 view 03 and A553.2 view 02; A550's POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND carries 'ALARM HORN AND STROBE (H)'; E101's symbol legend has a combination horn/strobe at 6'-8" AFF; E501 says 'notification: combination horn/strobes and strobes in corridors, public spaces, and guestrooms'. AGAINST: the Hilton-reviewed fire-alarm vendor submittal FA-1/FA-2/FA-3 draws NO horn and NO strobe in a standard key and schedules none to a guestroom — which would mean the low-frequency sounder bases under the two smoke detectors are the entire audible package. Precedence points at the SUBMITTAL: E500's own gap note says the E-series shows riser, sequence and symbols, not a device-by-device bill, and conflicts.md B1.9 records the same deferral; FA-1/FA-2/FA-3 IS that performance design and supersedes the E-series on device counts. Cutting the other way, FA-1's own audibility chart prints 'VISUAL REQUIRED' for sleeping rooms. There is also a mounting conflict: E101's legend says 6'-8" AFF while FA-1 schedules its notification appliances as CEILING units, 4"x4"x1.5". DO NOT RESOLVE THIS IN THE FIELD.
lines.src: FOR: A553.1 view 03 kn16 + H symbol · A553.2 view 01 kn16 · A553.2 view 02 kn16 + H symbol · A550 keynote legend 16 (verbatim) · A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND · E101 symbol legend (combination horn/strobe 6'-8" AFF) · E501. AGAINST: FA-1 schedules no horn/strobe to a guestroom · FA-2/FA-3 draw none in a standard key (verified on 303/305/307/311 and 304/306/308) · conflicts.md B1.9 · packages/fire-appliance.md section 2.4 limit 2
lines.verifyAtPunch: Answer one question in each room and photograph it: is there a horn or horn/strobe SEPARATE from the smoke detector — YES or NO, and how many in the suite? If yes — note horn-only vs horn+strobe, MEASURE and record the mounting height (6'-8" wall or ceiling), cover on and unpainted, and confirm it sounds on test. If no — confirm the LF sounder bases are carrying the audible duty at 75 dBA in BOTH rooms, and that there is no orphan capped box or blank plate left beside either SD.

lines.label: Ceiling strobes, System Sensor SCWLED — 2 at 177 cd in the habitable rooms plus 1 at 15 cd in the bathroom. COMMUNICATION-FEATURES (hearing-accessible) KEYS ONLY. Keynote 43 verbatim: 'ADDITIONAL HORN STROBE: LOCATED IN COMMUNICATION FEATURES BATHROOMS ONLY'
lines.where: Would be ceiling-mounted in the bedroom, the living room and the bathroom
lines.instanceNote: ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROW — 202 IS NOT ON THE IDENTIFIED HEARING-ACCESSIBLE LIST, BUT THAT LIST IS NOT CLOSED. G100.2 states 12 hearing-accessible keys building-wide. room_map.md has identified 8 of the 12 off the crossed-ear symbol on the plans, and the four it names on floor 2 are 209, 213, 216 and 218 — 202 is not among them. Four keys are still unknown. A hearing-accessible key carries THREE strobes (verified on rooms 309 and 313: two SCWLED at 177 cd, one at 15 cd in the bath, on circuits like PS3-3-1/2/3), so guessing the room list wrong is a three-device-per-room error. DO NOT DERIVE THE 12 FROM A UNIT MATRIX — conflicts.md A11 point 3 is open because A100's HI rows sum to 12 while G001's sum to 10 on a sheet that prints 'Provided 12', and A11 says in as many words: do not order 12 hearing/visual-alarm kits off G001's room-type rows. ALSO NOTE: mobility-accessible is NOT hearing-accessible — room 317, the King One Bedroom ACCESSIBLE, shows no strobes at all, while plain Queen-Queen 309 shows three. FA-2/FA-3 is the only source that settles which 12 rooms.
lines.src: A553 view 04 keyed note 43 · A550 keynote legend 43 (verbatim) and 16 · FA-1 schedule (SCWLED) · FA-3 rooms 309 and 313 read (3 strobes each, 177/177/15 cd) · FA-3 room 317 (no strobes) · G100.2 (12 hearing-accessible keys) · room_map.md (floor-2 HI at 209, 213, 216, 218) · conflicts.md A11 point 3
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look up in the bedroom, the living room and the bathroom: are there ceiling strobes — YES or NO, and how many? Expect NONE in 202. RECORD THE ANSWER either way. If strobes ARE installed, 202 is a communication-features key that nobody has on the list: record the candela markings, confirm the doorbell switch and the horn/strobe question with it, and get it onto the hearing-accessible room list before turnover.

lines.label: Sprinkler heads throughout the suite — HEAD COUNT FOR THIS ROOM TYPE IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY ANY DOCUMENT. Head model expected 'VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD' (FP-1 Description column), Thread 1/2", K-Factor 4.3.
lines.where: Ceilings throughout — bedroom (8'-3 3/8"), living room (8'-3 3/8"), dining nook, entry and closet (7'-3"). Bath is a separate line.
lines.instanceNote: QTY 1 IS A PLACEHOLDER, NOT A COUNT — THE COUNT IS THE DELIVERABLE FROM THIS LINE. This is a full DB GAP: the database holds sprinkler rows for other rooms and NONE AT ALL for 202. packages/fire-appliance.md section 1.4 lists King One Bedroom as an EXPLICIT PLACEHOLDER — 'NOT VERIFIED - a two-room suite almost certainly exceeds 3' — and the head model as an ASSUMPTION at about 90 percent (437 of 547 heads in the building are VK430 and both verified guestrooms are 100 percent VK430; no document states it for this type). PRESENCE IS HIGH, COUNT AND MODEL ARE NOT: FP-1's building note types every guestroom as light hazard, gives 18,183 SF protected per floor, and FA-0 independently prints 'THIS IS A FULLY SPRINKLERED BUILDING.' Only rooms 107 (Queen-Queen) and 108 (King Studio) were read head-by-head, at 3 heads each, and both are single-room studios — 202 is 26'-6" x 29'-0" clear across two rooms plus an entry leg. Do not carry 3 into this room. TRIM TYPE IS ALSO UNSETTLED: 'concealed pendent' is a READING of the 'PD' suffix, while A120 General Note I reads 'SPRINKLER HEADS IN CEILINGS IN PUBLIC AREAS TO BE CONCEALED. ALL OTHER HEADS TO BE SEMI-RECESSED' — a guest room is not a public area. Concealed means a flush cover plate; semi-recessed means a visible deflector. Two different looks and two different buys. No cover-plate finish or colour appears on any sheet. TO CLOSE: read the FP-1 through FP-4 room region for one King One Bedroom at 700-800 dpi, the way 107 and 108 were read — a document task, not an RFI.
lines.src: FP-1 Fire Sprinkler Shop Drawings, head schedule Description column (Texas Fire Services LLC, certified 03-26-2025, stamped City of Eagle Pass Fire Department) · packages/fire-appliance.md section 1.4 (King One Bedroom = PLACEHOLDER, NOT VERIFIED) and section 1.5 · A120 General Note I · A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND (sprinkler head / side wall sprinkler head symbols) · A530 General Note B ('smoke detectors, sprinklers and other emergency devices to be located per local code - indicated for design intent only')
lines.verifyAtPunch: COUNT EVERY SPRINKLER HEAD IN THE SUITE, ROOM BY ROOM — bedroom, living room, dining nook, entry, closet — and write down the number per room and the total. That count is the single most valuable thing on this walk for this room type, because no document has it. At each head: RECORD the trim actually installed, FLUSH COVER PLATE (concealed) or ESCUTCHEON WITH VISIBLE DEFLECTOR (semi-recessed), and the plate finish, and photograph one. Confirm every head is seated, square, UNPAINTED, with no ceiling texture run over the plate, and that nothing is stored or mounted inside its clearance. Read the model off one plate if it is legible.

lines.label: Guest bathroom sprinkler head — confirm-absence row. No head was drawn in either verified guest bath.
lines.where: Bath ceiling, 7'-3" AFF
lines.instanceNote: ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROW SO THE WALKER KNOWS WHETHER TO EXPECT A HEAD — without it they will either false-flag its absence or walk past one that is not on the drawings. THE OBSERVATION IS FROM TWO STUDIO BATHS, NOT FROM THIS ONE: rooms 107 and 108 were read at 700-800 dpi and no head is drawn in either bathroom, but both are A530 studio baths. THE KING ONE BEDROOM BATH IS A DIFFERENT AND MUCH LARGER ROOM — A531 gives it 12'-0 1/2" x 9'-0 1/2" clear with a 5'-0" shower, against the studio bath's 6'-3 1/2" width — and A531 itself states that sprinkler layout in the bath is not answerable from that sheet. So the absence is UNVERIFIED for this type. WRITE 'no head drawn', NEVER 'no head required' — the governing standard is itself open: FP-1 (the City-stamped submittal) designs to NFPA 13-2021 while the G-series code analysis says 13R, and A530 General Note B says emergency devices are 'INDICATED FOR DESIGN INTENT ONLY'.
lines.src: FP-1, room regions 107 (QQ) and 108 (King Studio) read at 700-800 dpi — no head drawn in either bathroom · A531 (suite bath 12'-0 1/2" x 9'-0 1/2" clear; 'not answerable from this sheet: ceiling, exhaust or sprinkler layout in the bath') · A530 General Note B · packages/fire-appliance.md section 1.4 · coordination_issues.md K-03 (NFPA 13 vs 13R)
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look up in the bath and RECORD PRESENT or ABSENT. If a head IS installed, photograph it, log the room and read the model off the plate — it is not on FP-1 for this type and it belongs on the as-built and in the hydraulic record. Remove nothing, and do not write up an absence as a deficiency.

lines.label: Carbon monoxide detector — NONE is scheduled to any guest room. Confirm-absence row.
lines.where: Would be a ceiling or wall device in the sleeping room
lines.instanceNote: ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROW. The vendor submittal's verified read of a standard key states it plainly: no horn/strobe, NO CO DETECTOR and no pull station in a guest room, and FA-1 schedules none to a guestroom. The building has no in-room fuel-burning appliance — the PTACs are electric 208 V and the kitchenette is a microwave, a refrigerator and a dishwasher — so the absence is consistent. Recorded so the walker does not chase one, and so that if one IS found it gets logged rather than ignored.
lines.src: FA-1 Fire Alarm Equipment Schedule (no CO device scheduled to a guestroom) · FA-2/FA-3 verified standard keys (no CO detector) · packages/fire-appliance.md section 2.2 · M201 (PTAC 208/1/60, electric)
